title: Fabrication of high-quality glass microfluidic devices for bioanalytical and space flight applications
author: Golozar, Chu, et al.

steps.title: Clean borofloat wafers
steps.instruction: Thoroughly clean both sides of each Borofloat glass wafer before any deposition.

substeps.instruction: Rinse wafer with deionized water and NovaClean liquid to remove grease and particulates.
Place wafer in an ultrasonic acetone bath with the etched side facing down.
Identify the polished side (ground) and keep the opposite side pristine for later channel definition.
Immerse wafer in piranha solution for 10 min at 80 °C to eliminate organic residues.
Perform a quick‑dump rinse (QDR) followed by a spin‑rinse‑dry (SRD) cycle for final rinsing and drying.

steps.title: Deposit a‑Si via LPCVD
steps.instruction: Deposit a 2000 Å amorphous silicon layer on the cleaned wafers using the Tystar16 LPCVD furnace.

substeps.instruction: Select wafers free of scratches or chips and confirm they have completed the standard cleaning procedure.
Load the wafers into the Tystar16 furnace (compatible with 4" and 6" wafers, up to 25 wafers per run).
Set the LPCVD parameters (as previously optimized on dummy wafers) to achieve a 2000 Å a‑Si film thickness.
Run the deposition cycle and allow the furnace to cool before unloading the wafers.

steps.title: Prepare wafer for photoresist
steps.instruction: Condition the a‑Si coated wafers to ensure good photoresist adhesion.

substeps.instruction: Blow nitrogen gas over the wafer surfaces to remove any remaining particulates.
Perform a dehydration bake in an oven at 120 °C for 30 min.
Follow with a hot‑plate dehydration bake at 200 °C for 5 min.
Prime the wafer with vapor HMDS using the standard recipe: total 11 min, including a 2 min priming period with no pump and the required purge cycles.
Proceed to photoresist coating immediately after HMDS priming (the HMDS layer remains effective for about one hour).

steps.title: Spin coat S1818 photoresist
steps.instruction: Apply a 2 µm thick layer of Shipley S1818 positive photoresist on the wafer.

substeps.instruction: Place the wafer on the spinner chuck with the superior (pristine) surface facing up.
During the first 5 s of spin, dispense photoresist directly from the bottle onto the wafer, covering roughly 90 % of the surface; avoid introducing bubbles.
Spin at 500 rpm with an acceleration of 100 rpm/s for 5 s to spread the resist.
Immediately increase to 2500 rpm with an acceleration of 500 rpm/s and spin for 25 s (total spin time 30 s) to achieve a 2 µm film.
After spinning, let the wafer rest on the chuck for 15–20 s to let the resist firm up.
Transfer the wafer to the soft‑bake station.

steps.title: Soft bake photoresist
steps.instruction: Semi‑harden the spun‑on photoresist before exposure.

substeps.instruction: Place the wafer on a hot plate set to 120 °C for 2.5 min.
Remove the wafer and cool it on a cooling block for 10–15 s.

steps.title: Protect backside for silicon etch
steps.instruction: Apply protective tape to the wafer backside before reactive‑ion etching.

substeps.instruction: Lay a sheet of Vinyl Surface Protection Tape on a flat surface.
Place the wafer on the tape with the back (silicon‑coated) side contacting the tape.
Trim excess tape around the wafer edges using a razor blade.
Flip the wafer over and use the back of the blade or a hard‑plastic card to push any trapped air bubbles toward the edges, ensuring full tape contact.
